thesis: Slop is not bad writing. Slop is a decision nobody made.

method.corpus_rule: agent-authored .md/.mdx/.rst/.txt prose >= 60 words; vendored libraries, licences, node_modules and asset dirs excluded by name
method.frame_rule: a sentence is FRAME when >=60% of its 5-grams (entity-masked: numbers, tickers, handles, dates, versions, CVEs collapsed to slots) already appear in at least 3 other documents
method.anchor_rule: verifiable anchors = urls, handles, tickers, CVE ids, issue numbers, semver, dates, quantities with units, currency, 0x addresses, paths, code
method.specificity_rule: anchor density per 1,000 words measured over NON-FRAME sentences only, so a document made entirely of inherited text scores 0 by construction

corpus.binary_note: binary artifacts are not scored. Reducto is the layer that makes them auditable at all, and its layout boxes are what let slop be located per region

Structured audit logging for mutations and security events.
Currently writes to `console` — Prisma persistence is planned (see upgrade path below).
| Export | Signature | Description |
| `logMutation` | `(action, actor, target, details) => void` | Log a state-changing operation (create, update, delete).
| `logSecurityEvent` | `(eventType, details) => void` | Log auth failures, rate-limit hits, invalid input, or suspicious activity.
| `logApiAccess` | `(method, path, ip, userAgent, statusCode) => void` | Log inbound API requests.
Every log entry includes a `requestId` (UUID v4) and ISO timestamp.
**Event types for `logSecurityEvent`**
`auth_failure` | `rate_limit` | `invalid_input` | `suspicious_activity`
> **⚠️ Persistence Upgrade Plan:** Console-only logging means security events (auth failures, rate-limit hits, suspicious activity) are lost on process restart or PM2 reload.
The planned upgrade path is:
Add an `AuditLog` model to `devio-x402-server/prisma/schema.prisma` with fields:
`id`, `requestId`, `type` (`mutation` | `security` | `access`), `action`, `actor`, `target`, `details` (JSON), `ip`, `userAgent`, `statusCode`, `createdAt`.
Update `audit-logger.ts` to accept an optional Prisma client and write rows when available, falling back to `console` for backwards compatibility.
Expose the persisted log via the existing `GET /api/admin/audit-log` endpoint (currently stubs).
Add a retention policy (e.g.
auto-purge entries older than 90 days) to keep the table bounded.
> Until this upgrade lands, treat audit logs as best-effort diagnostics only — do NOT rely on them for compliance or incident response.

spans.t: The `openclaw-bridge` skill connects D0xed Dev to the [OpenClaw](https://clawn.ch) agent ecosystem.
It implements the **OpenClaw Agent Card v1** protocol, enabling other agents to discover D0xed Dev, register with the hub, and request task collaborations.
An **agent card** is a standardised JSON manifest (`$schema:
https://openclaw.ai/schemas/agent-card/v1.json`) that describes an agent's identity, capabilities, pricing, and collaboration preferences.
D0xed Dev's card lives at:
**HTTP endpoint:** `GET /api/agent-card` (Express) and `GET /api/agent-card` (Next.js)
Agents propose tasks using `POST /api/collaborate`.
The body must contain:
{ /* AgentCardV1 */ },
"scam-analysis | token-screening | social-amplification",
Proposals are stored in PostgreSQL via Prisma and can be retrieved via `GET /api/collaborations` (x402-gated at 0.01 USDC).
**Discover** — Fetch `GET https://api.d0xeddev.com/api/agent-card` to learn D0xed Dev's capabilities and pricing.
**Register** — `POST /api/agents` with a signed wallet payload to join the hub registry.
**Collaborate** — `POST /api/collaborate` with your agent card and a task proposal.
**Check status** — Poll `GET /api/collaborations` (requires 0.01 USDC x402 payment).

| `scripts/agent-card-server.ts` | `getAgentCard()`, `validateIncomingAgentCard()`, `enrichAgentCardWithLiveData()` |
